Archiving works end to end. Screenshots under `prototypes/` (live: **http://maker:4001/archive.html**).

**Main list with an Archive action** (`shot-27-archive-mainlist.png`)
Each bookmark has a **🗄 Archive** action alongside "Mark finished". Your main switch (To read / Finished / All) shows only *active* bookmarks, and off to the right there's an unobtrusive **🗄 Archived (2)** entry — out of the way, so it doesn't clutter the library.

**Archiving removes it from the main list** (`shot-29-archive-after-archiving.png`)
I archived "How to roast vegetables perfectly" from the **All** view — it immediately disappears from the main list (which now shows 3), and the **Archived** count ticks up to 3. It's tucked away, not deleted.

**The Archived view** (`shot-28-archive-view.png`)
Opening **Archived** shows the kept-aside bookmarks with a reassuring line ("kept out of your main list but never lost") and a **↩ Restore** on each, which returns the bookmark to your main list in the state it was.

Two things I want your judgment on, because I picked a direction:

- I treated **archiving as separate from Finished** — a bookmark can be To-read or Finished *and* be archived; archiving just hides it from the main views. Archived is reached through its own **Archived** entry, not mixed into the To read/Finished/All switch. Does that match your mental model, or did you picture "archived" as simply another status in the same switch?
- **Should archived bookmarks still turn up when you search?** I can see it either way: exclude them from search so search stays focused on your active library, *or* still find them (perhaps marked "Archived") so nothing you kept is ever truly hidden. Which fits how you'd want to "keep without cluttering"?
